title: Claude Opus 4.8 — Effort Controls and Dynamic Workflows
content:
## Overview

Claude Opus 4.8, released May 28, 2026, is Anthropic's current top-tier production model. It builds on Opus 4.7 with improved agentic benchmarks, a new effort-control system, and dynamic workflows for Claude Code. Pricing is unchanged from Opus 4.7, and the model is identified as `claude-opus-4-8` across the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry.

---

## Benchmark Improvements

Compared to Opus 4.7:

| Benchmark | Opus 4.7 | Opus 4.8 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Agentic coding | 64.3% | 69.2% | +4.9pp |
| Multidisciplinary reasoning with tools | 54.7% | 57.9% | +3.2pp |
| Knowledge work score | 1753 | 1890 | +7.8% |

Anthropic describes the model as having "sharper judgement, more honesty about its progress, and the ability to work independently for longer than its predecessors."

---

## Effort Controls

Users on claude.ai can now configure how much effort Claude applies to a task. Rather than always running at maximum throughput, Claude calibrates the depth of its reasoning — useful for quick, low-stakes queries where a fast, lighter response is preferable over a deep one.

In Claude Code, Opus 4.8 is configured for **high effort by default** on Max, Team Premium, Enterprise pay-as-you-go, and Anthropic API accounts.

---

## Dynamic Workflows (Claude Code)

Dynamic workflows are the headline Claude Code feature shipping with Opus 4.8. Available in research preview in the Claude Code CLI, Desktop app, and VS Code extension for Max, Team, and Enterprise plans — and on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry.

**What they enable:** A single script can orchestrate numerous sub-agents in parallel, each handling a slice of a large-scale problem. This makes multi-agent orchestration declarative and scriptable rather than requiring custom coordination code.

**Typical use case:** A large codebase refactor where one coordinator agent divides work across hundreds of files, spins up sub-agents for each module, collects results, and merges them — all driven by a single workflow definition.

Dynamic workflows build on Claude Code's existing multi-agent support (which already allowed subagent spawning via the Agent tool) but extend it to support very large parallelism from a single entry point.

---

## Agent View

Alongside dynamic workflows, Claude Code shipped **agent view** — a new CLI interface for managing multiple sessions from one terminal. Features:

- Start agents and send them to the background
- Peek at status and last response without entering a session
- Jump back into a session only when input is needed
- Background sessions (started via `claude --bg` or agent view) appear in the resume picker, marked with `bg`

Rate limits on Claude Code were also doubled with the Opus 4.8 rollout.

---

## Self-Hosted Sandboxes and MCP Tunnels

Two infrastructure features for the Managed Agents platform released alongside Opus 4.8:

- **Self-hosted sandboxes (public beta):** Tool execution moves to your own infrastructure or a managed provider, while the agent loop stays on Anthropic's servers. Your network policies, audit logging, and security tooling apply to all tool calls.
- **MCP tunnels (research preview):** Agents can reach MCP servers inside private networks without exposing them to the public internet, via a lightweight gateway.

---

## Messages API: In-Flight Updates

The Messages API now supports real-time updates to the messages array *while an agent is active* — allowing developers to change instructions, adjust permissions, modify token limits, or update context during a running task, without disrupting prompt caching.

---

## Claude Platform on AWS

Also launched with Opus 4.8: the Claude Platform on AWS, described as a first-of-its-kind offering where Anthropic operates the service directly and all native Claude API features are available from day one, with data processed outside the AWS boundary.
